caption:
Google's own Gemini help pages say a subset of data from connected apps like Gmail and Drive is reviewed by human reviewers.
Reviewers can see excerpts, summaries and inferences from relevant emails and files, and reviewed chats are kept for up to three years.
Google's advice: don't connect apps that hold confidential information. Turning off Keep Activity stops future chats from being reviewed.

Would you still connect your Gmail to Gemini?

site_article.headline: Google says human reviewers may see Gmail and Drive data connected to Gemini
site_article.dek: Google's Gemini help pages warn that a subset of data from connected apps is reviewed by people, as a GitHub write-up claims Gemini pulls in emails and files without being asked.
site_article.summary: Google's Gemini help pages say a subset of data from connected apps such as Gmail and Drive is reviewed by human reviewers, and that reviewed chats are kept for up to three years. A GitHub write-up circulating since November 9, 2026 says Gemini can pull personal emails and files into a chat without an explicit request.
site_article.seo_title: Gemini human reviewers can see Gmail and Drive excerpts
site_article.seo_description: Google's Gemini help pages say people review a subset of data from connected Gmail and Drive. What reviewers see and how to stop it.
site_article.answer_summary: Yes. Google says a subset of Gemini data from connected apps like Gmail and Drive is reviewed by human reviewers. Turning off Keep Activity stops future chats from being reviewed.
site_article.hero_alt: Portrait of a man with a serious expression, photographed at a public event.

paragraphs.text: Google's help documentation for Gemini says that a subset of data processed through Connected Apps, the feature that links Gemini to services such as Gmail, Drive, Calendar and Docs, is reviewed by human reviewers. The page tells users not to connect their apps to Gemini if those apps contain confidential information. The wording drew wide attention on November 9 and 10, 2026, after a GitHub write-up about it spread online.

According to the Connected Apps help page, reviewers assess whether Gemini's responses were low quality, inaccurate or harmful and suggest better ones. The material they may see includes interactions, summaries, excerpts and inferences drawn from relevant emails and files, along with the user's prompts and Gemini's replies. The page adds that human reviewers may also review some of a user's Gmail inbox or Google Photos media.

Google also states on the same page that Gemini does not train generative AI models directly on a user's Gmail inbox, Drive, Contacts, Calendar or other Workspace apps. Gemini Apps activity, which includes data from connected apps, can be used to improve Google services, including model training, when the Keep Activity setting is on.

The Gemini Apps Privacy Hub, last updated on October 26, 2026, says reviewers include trained staff from Google's service providers. Chats are disconnected from the user's account before they are sent to those providers, and reviewed chats are retained for up to three years. The hub says that turning off Keep Activity stops future chats from being reviewed to improve Google services.

The attention started with a public GitHub repository by a pseudonymous author. The author argues that Google promised in 2023 that personal content from Gmail, Docs and Drive would not be seen by human reviewers, and says the related blog post was edited on October 16. In the author's tests, a casual question about internet prices led Gemini to retrieve an internet bill from the author's inbox without an @Gmail or @Drive tag.

The repository describes four different outcomes from similar prompts: no retrieval, a general summary, a partial quotation, or the full text of a file. StartupHub.ai, which reported on the findings, noted that the tests come from one unverified set of experiments and that Google had not commented beyond its help text.

The core facts here come from Google's own documentation, not from the leak claims. What changes the picture for ordinary users is the combination of two features: Gemini can reach into connected mail and files to answer everyday questions, and a share of those conversations can be read by people. Users who connected Gmail for convenience may not have expected that excerpts of their messages could end up in a review queue, even with the account details removed.

Google gives users two controls in its documentation. Connected apps can be managed in the Personal Intelligence settings, and Keep Activity can be switched off. Google notes that disconnecting an app does not delete data already saved in Gemini Apps Activity.

Watch whether Google responds directly to the GitHub claims about background retrieval, and whether privacy regulators or larger outlets test how often Gemini pulls in full emails and files without a direct request.
